conclusion.original: Fix a positive time horizon T, a coarse level m and a fine level n at least m. Choose a coarse grid point τ. For any two real paths X and Y on nonnegative time, the fine-grid sum of products of their stopped increments equals the fine-grid prefix sum of their original increment products through τ. Formula: \sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1}\bigl(X_{\min(\tau,t_{i+1})}-X_{\min(\tau,t_i)}\bigr)\bigl(Y_{\min(\tau,t_{i+1})}-Y_{\min(\tau,t_i)}\bigr)=\sum_{i:\ t_{i+1}\le \tau}(X_{t_{i+1}}-X_{t_i})(Y_{t_{i+1}}-Y_{t_i}).
conclusion.reconstructed: Let tau=kT/2^m and t_i=iT/2^n for i=0,...,2^n. Then ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(X(min(tau,t_{i+1}))-X(min(tau,t_i)))(Y(min(tau,t_{i+1}))-Y(min(tau,t_i))) = ∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}1_{t_{i+1}≤tau}(X(t_{i+1})-X(t_i))(Y(t_{i+1})-Y(t_i)).
conclusion.evidence: The displayed source formula agrees with the expanded target at AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/DyadicCutoffIncrements.lean:10 and the independent reconstruction. Fin(2^m+1) includes both endpoints; hmn ensures each fine cell lies wholly before or after tau. The two branches rewrite both minima and the inclusive indicator without any path-regularity premise.
